standard.title: Segment phonemes in words
standard.description: segment words into separate phonemes (sounds) including consonant blends or clusters at the beginnings and ends of words (phonological awareness)
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and generate rhyming words, identify syllables and segment single-syllable CVC words into onset and rime at Foundation level (AC9EFLY15). They have not yet segmented words fully into individual phonemes, particularly those containing consonant blends or clusters.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students segment words into all separate phonemes including consonant blends and clusters at word beginnings and ends.

nodes.label: Phoneme segmentation in simple words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can segment single-syllable words into all individual phonemes in sequence.
nodes.minimum_width: Segment at least three single-syllable words (including CVC and CVCC patterns) into individual phonemes in order.
nodes.typical_width: Segment single-syllable words into all phonemes in sequence, including words with initial and final consonants, across varied vowel patterns.
wider: Segment words with four phonemes and confirm count
Compare segmentation of words with similar spelling but different phoneme counts
nodes.hinge_reason: Accurate single-word phoneme segmentation is definitionally prerequisite for N2 and N3 — students who cannot segment simple words cannot isolate individual consonants within blends.

response_modes.reason: Accurate phoneme segmentation requires repeated practice — students often blend phonemes rather than cleanly separating each one. Segmentation is a foundational decoding skill that underpins spelling and must be automated.

success_criteria: Student segments a single-syllable word into correct individual phonemes in order
Student counts phonemes accurately (not letters) in a given word

nodes.label: Segmenting words with initial consonant blends
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can segment words that begin with consonant blends or clusters (e.g. sp-, st-, bl-, cr-) into their individual phonemes.
nodes.minimum_width: Segment at least two words with initial consonant blends (e.g. 'spoon', 'fist') into all phonemes.
nodes.typical_width: Segment a range of words with initial consonant blends — including two- and three-consonant clusters — into individual phonemes, saying sounds in order.
wider: Sort words by their initial consonant blend and compare the phoneme count
Compare segmenting a word with an initial blend versus without — e.g. 'lip' vs 'slip'
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot segment initial blends into separate phonemes will merge blend consonants in N3 final blend segmentation — the strategy of treating each consonant individually must be established before the harder final-position work.

response_modes.reason: Initial consonant blends are segmented differently depending on the cluster (sp- vs str- vs bl-). Students need exposure to a range of initial blend types to build a flexible segmentation strategy rather than a pattern-specific one.

success_criteria: Student correctly segments a word with an initial consonant blend, treating each consonant as a separate phoneme
Student says phonemes in correct order for a blend word

nodes.label: Segmenting words with final consonant blends
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can segment words with final consonant blends or clusters into their individual phonemes.
nodes.minimum_width: Segment at least two words with final consonant blends (e.g. 'fist', 'lamp') into all phonemes.
nodes.typical_width: Segment words with final consonant blends — including common patterns such as -st, -nd, -mp, -nk — into individual phonemes.
wider: Segment words with both initial and final consonant blends (e.g. 'stamp', 'blend')
Discuss how segmenting words with final blends helps with spelling
nodes.hinge_reason: Complete phoneme segmentation — including final blends — is prerequisite for AC9E1LY10 phoneme manipulation; students cannot delete, substitute or add phonemes within blend positions they have not learned to isolate.

response_modes.reason: Final consonant blends are harder to segment than initial blends for most students — the end of the word receives less articulatory attention. Repeated practice with final blends before moving to both-ends blending is important.

success_criteria: Student correctly segments a word with a final consonant blend
Student does not merge the final blend consonants into a single sound
